title: Pro vs Home Jigs
body_html:
For many frame builders the jig is their most essential bit of kit. It allows a frame builder to align a frame, ensure the wheels spin and check if everything is squared up. At Bamboo Bicycle Club, we’ve been building and designing custom bamboo specific jigs for the last 10 years. So for our first series finale live #workshopwednesdays session, we introduced our audience to our workshop and home build jigs! We took our audience through some of our best practices and how to use these jigs.

One of the most common questions BBC builders ask is: do I need a professional workshop jig, or will the home jig that comes with my kit be sufficient? The answer depends on your goals — but for the vast majority of builds, the BBC home jig produces results that are indistinguishable from frames built on professional tooling.

The BBC home jig is a flat-pack single-use system designed specifically for the kit build process. It sets up quickly, accommodates a range of frame geometries, and holds tubes in alignment throughout the critical curing phase. For builders making a single frame, or even two or three frames over time, the home jig is the right choice: it is cost-effective, requires no permanent workshop space, and is designed around the BBC build sequence.

Professional workshop jigs — used in the BBC's London studio and available for volume builders — are steel-framed, adjustable systems that can be reset to different geometries quickly and withstand many build cycles. They offer greater precision for small geometry adjustments and are easier to use when building multiple frames back to back. For franchise holders and professional frame builders, a workshop jig is an investment that pays back over time.

"Bamboo Bicycle Club follows a niche-manufacturing business model that prioritises knowledge-sharing over profit-making retail, charging for workshops and kits rather than pre-made products."

— Huck Magazine, 2023

The BBC's guidance: start with the home jig. If you build your first frame and want to continue building — whether for yourself, for sale, or as part of a BBC franchise — the upgrade path to a workshop jig is straightforward. The BBC team can advise on jig selection based on your specific build goals.
